Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old female with several months of dry, cracked, itchy palmar skin affecting work-related activities; suspected dermatitis/contact dermatitis related to cleaning products; plan includes protective gloves, topical steroid and emollient, with follow-up in 10–14 days or sooner if symptoms worsen.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Soreness and cracking of skin on hands, primarily palms; dryness noted on legs but milder; itching present; intermittent bleeding with scratching.
- Timeline: Symptoms started about 3–4 months ago; gradually worse, now painful and limiting ability to work.
- Exposures/initiating factors: Works as a housekeeper in a hotel; inconsistent glove use; recent job change ~4 months ago; exposure to bathroom/cleaning products may be related.
- Exacerbating factors: Cleaning products; lack of glove use.
- Relieving factors: No specific relief reported; over-the-counter creams tried without benefit.
- Associated symptoms: Itching; occasional bleeding with scratching; no fever, nausea, vomiting, abdominal/bowel symptoms, or urinary symptoms.
- General health: Eating and appetite well; no systemic symptoms reported.
- Systems review: No other organ system complaints documented.

Past Medical History:
- Diabetes mellitus type 2; on metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- No prior skin diseases diagnosed; no eczema/dermatitis diagnosed.

Medications:
- Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- No allergies reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: Hotel housekeeper; variable glove use; exposure to cleaning products.
- Exposure: Cleaning products used in bathrooms; not always gloves worn.
- Smoking: None.
- Alcohol: Minimal (a couple of pints per week).
- Living/other factors: Recently changed job.

Family History:
- Diabetes noted in family; no other skin problems or relevant conditions mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Skin findings (as described in history): Palms with dry, cracked skin; itching; intermittent bleeding with scratching.
- No other physical examination findings documented.

Investigations:
- No laboratory tests or imaging performed or ordered.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Dermatitis / contact dermatitis (likely related to occupational exposure to cleaning products and inconsistent glove use).
  - Plan:
    - Advise avoidance of triggers and consistent use of gloves during cleaning.
    - Initiate topical corticosteroid cream to reduce inflammation (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Initiate stronger emollients to moisturize skin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Follow-up in 10–14 days; return sooner if symptoms worsen or spreading occurs.
    - If no improvement after 1–2 weeks, reassess and consider additional therapies.
    - Prescription for topical treatments to be sent to pharmacy (drug names/doses not specified in transcript).
- General plan: Educate on skin care and protection; monitor progress and adjust treatment if needed.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vitals (no vitals documented).
  - Specific medication dosages, routes, and frequencies for Metformin and prescribed topicals (not documented).
  - Explicit allergy history beyond “no allergies” stated.
- Internal conflicts: None detected in the transcript.
- Transcript quality: Clear clinical discussion; some filler dialogue, but content is coherent and sufficient for this note.
